items.bold: TRUMP ESCALATED: Iran response now "PIECE OF GARBAGE." Aides more seriously considering major combat. Frustrated with Iranian leadership "division."
items.text: CBS News (17 hours ago) and CNN confirmed: Trump escalated his language — calling Iran's response a "piece of garbage" in addition to "totally unacceptable." CNN sources: "Trump has grown increasingly frustrated with how the Iranians are handling negotiations to end the war, and some Trump aides say that he is now more seriously considering a resumption of major combat operations than he has in recent weeks. Trump has grown impatient with the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz, as well as what he perceives as division in Iranian leadership that is preventing them from making substantial concessions on nuclear talks." The "division in Iranian leadership" perception is analytically significant: Trump believes Iran's political and military wings are not unified, making negotiations unreliable. This frustration drives the escalating rhetoric before Beijing — Trump wants Xi to know he is serious about combat resumption.

items.bold: TRUMP-XI BEIJING THURSDAY — White House set LOW EXPECTATIONS on Iran. Wang Yi: open Hormuz "AS SOON AS POSSIBLE." China wants something in return.
items.text: CNBC (8 hours ago), Chatham House (18 hours ago), and CSIS confirmed: Trump heads to Beijing Thursday for his first China visit since 2017. White House has set low expectations on Iran specifically — the administration "seems determined not to let differences on Iran overshadow efforts to make headway on other difficult matters" including trade, rare earths, Taiwan, and AI. Wang Yi (China's top diplomat) has called for Hormuz to be opened "as soon as possible" in talks with his Iranian counterpart. Chatham House's Ahmed Aboudouh: China is "very cautious, risk-averse, and they don't want to be involved in anything that would drag them into something that they don't consider their problem." China has leverage but "will want something from the US in return, if it is to use it." The agenda spans trade, technology, rare earth export controls, Taiwan, the Iran war, and AI. CSIS: "US will focus on economy and Iran; China will seek stability and progress on Taiwan."

items.bold: IRAN AMBASSADOR TO CHINA: "Relationship TOO STRONG for US to overcome." Supreme Leader advisor warns Trump. Ghalibaf: "Prepared for every option."
items.text: CNN and CBS confirmed: Iran's ambassador to China, Abdolreza Rahmani Fazli, posted on X on Tuesday pressing Tehran's case with Beijing, saying the relationship between Iran and China is "too strong for the US to overcome." An advisor to Iran's Supreme Leader warned Trump "should not mistake the current lack of fighting between the US and Iran as a victory" as he heads to Beijing. Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf stated Iran is "prepared for every option" as negotiations with the US remain stalled. CNBC analysis: "China gains a positional advantage" — Beijing is Iran's largest trade partner and top oil buyer. Iran's ambassador to China posting publicly signals Iran is actively lobbying Beijing not to concede to US pressure. China must choose between its economic relationship with Iran and its strategic relationship with the US. The summit outcome depends on what Xi decides to prioritise.

items.bold: ISRAEL SENT IRON DOME BATTERIES TO UAE. Israeli strikes South Lebanon killed 6. Israel-UAE security architecture deepening.
items.text: CBS News (17 hours ago) confirmed: Israel sent Iron Dome anti-missile batteries and personnel to operate them to the UAE to defend the country during the Iran war. US Ambassador Huckabee confirmed this at an event in Tel Aviv: "I'd like to say a word of appreciation for the UAE, the first Abraham Accord member." The Israel-UAE Iron Dome deployment is a significant new development: it formalises an Israel-UAE security partnership as a direct response to Iran's drone attacks on UAE. This creates a new regional security architecture — Israel is now effectively defending Gulf Arab states against Iran using its proven missile defense technology. Separately: Israeli strikes Monday night on a house in Kfar Dounine in south Lebanon killed six people and wounded seven (Lebanon NNA confirmed). Fighting continues despite Lebanon ceasefire agreement.

items.bold: BRENT $100-104 Tuesday. US gas $4.50. Diesel +61% since last May. US midterms <6 months. "Higher prices baked in."
items.text: CNBC (8 hours ago) confirmed: Brent crude traded $100-104 range Tuesday. US national average gasoline: $4.50/gallon (AAA Tuesday) — Brent up 44% since start of war, still below Ukraine 2022 highs. Diesel up 61% since last May. CNBC: "The bottom line is that higher energy prices are baked in for the foreseeable future." The 2026 midterm elections are less than six months away — "a crucial referendum on Trump and the Republican Party as they seek to retain a lock on both chambers in Congress." With gas at $4.50 and diesel at +61%: every week without a Hormuz deal costs Republicans seats. Trump's political incentive to get a Beijing deal on Iran is at its maximum. Aramco CEO noted mines clearing timeline was not even included in the months-long normalisation forecast — adding further delay risk to any deal.

military.t: TRUMP: Iran Response "PIECE OF GARBAGE." Aides Considering Major Combat. Frustrated with Iranian Leadership "Division."
military.d: CBS News (17hr ago) and CNN confirmed: Trump escalated his language — calling Iran's response a "piece of garbage" after previously calling it "totally unacceptable" and "stupid." CNN sources: Trump has grown increasingly frustrated with Iranian leadership, specifically perceiving "division in Iranian leadership that is preventing them from making substantial concessions on nuclear talks." Trump aides are now more seriously considering a resumption of major combat operations than at any point since the ceasefire. The Iran advisor to Iran's Supreme Leader warned Trump "should not mistake the current lack of fighting between the US and Iran as a victory." Ghalibaf: Iran "prepared for every option." The escalating language from both sides — "piece of garbage" + "prepared for every option" — signals the ceasefire is under its most severe political strain since April 8.

military.t: TRUMP-XI BEIJING SUMMIT THURSDAY — White House Low Expectations on Iran. Wang Yi: Open Hormuz "AS SOON AS POSSIBLE."
military.d: CNBC (8hr ago), Chatham House, CSIS confirmed: Trump arrives in Beijing Thursday — first China visit since 2017. White House set LOW EXPECTATIONS specifically on Iran at this summit — the administration wants to prevent Iran from overshadowing progress on trade, rare earths, Taiwan, and AI. Wang Yi (China top diplomat) has called for Hormuz to be opened "as soon as possible" in talks with Araghchi. Chatham House (Ahmed Aboudouh): China "very cautious, risk-averse" — sent subtle message of discontent to BOTH Iran (for closing Hormuz) AND the US (for the blockade). "They don't want to be involved in anything that would drag them into something that they don't consider their problem." China will want something from the US in return for applying pressure on Iran. CSIS: US focuses on economy and Iran; China seeks stability and progress on Taiwan. The deal China wants = US concessions on Taiwan or trade in exchange for Iran pressure.

military.t: IRAN Lobbying Beijing — Ambassador: Relationship "TOO STRONG for US." Advisor: Trump "Should Not Mistake Lack of Fighting as Victory."

An advisor to Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned Trump "should not mistake the current lack of fighting between the US and Iran as a victory" as he heads to Beijing. Ghalibaf: Iran "prepared for every option." CNBC analysis: "China gains a positional advantage — Beijing is Iran's largest trade partner and the top buyer of its oil." Iran is simultaneously: (1) submitting proposals via Pakistan, (2) warning Trump not to feel victorious, (3) lobbying China not to pressure it, (4) preparing for every option militarily. This is Iran's comprehensive diplomatic and military positioning before the Beijing summit.

assessment.headline: DAY 75, 7AM WED: TRUMP: Iran response "PIECE OF GARBAGE." AIDES CONSIDERING MAJOR COMBAT RESUMPTION. TRUMP-XI BEIJING THURSDAY — LOW EXPECTATIONS ON IRAN. IRAN LOBBYING CHINA NOT TO CONCEDE. ISRAEL IRON DOME IN UAE. ARAGHCHI BRICS DELHI THURSDAY. OMC HIKE IMMINENT. Most consequential 48 hours of the war: THURSDAY-FRIDAY.
assessment.body:
Wednesday 7:00 AM IST. Day 75. The war arrives at its most consequential 48 hours.

TRUMP'S ESCALATING LANGUAGE
"Totally unacceptable" (Sunday) → "stupid" (Monday) → "piece of garbage" (Tuesday)
Each escalation signals frustration deepening and military patience thinning.
Trump aides: more seriously considering major combat resumption than at any point since ceasefire.
Why: Trump perceives "division in Iranian leadership" preventing nuclear concessions.
Iran advisor to Supreme Leader: Trump "should not mistake lack of fighting as victory."

THE BEIJING SUMMIT — WHAT ANALYSTS EXPECT
White House: LOW EXPECTATIONS on Iran.
Trump agenda: economy, trade, rare earths, Taiwan, AI — Iran as one item among many.
Wang Yi: Hormuz should open "as soon as possible."
Chatham House: China "risk-averse, cautious" — will want something from US in return.
China leverage: Iran's largest trade partner + top oil buyer.
US leverage: trade concessions, Taiwan policy, sanctions easing.
The deal China wants: US flexibility on Taiwan or trade for Chinese pressure on Iran.
Probability of decisive Beijing outcome on Iran: low-to-medium.
But even a signal that China will pressure Iran on nuclear = Brent falls $8-12.

IRAN'S BEIJING LOBBYING
Iran ambassador to China posted Tuesday: relationship "too strong for US to overcome."
This is Iran telling Xi: "Don't help Trump." Simultaneously:
Iran advisor warns Trump not to feel victorious.
Ghalibaf: "prepared for every option."
Iran is playing both tracks — diplomatic proposals via Pakistan, military preparation, lobbying Beijing.

ISRAEL-UAE SECURITY ARCHITECTURE
Iron Dome batteries now operating in UAE — first time Israeli military technology actively defending a Gulf Arab state.
This is the Abraham Accords delivering strategic results.
Iran's drone attacks on UAE now face Israeli missile defense.
New Gulf security architecture: US-Israel-UAE-Saudi aligned against Iran.

INDIA'S THURSDAY — THE MOMENT
Araghchi in Delhi at BRICS: EAM Jaishankar must raise:
→ Indian tanker coordination in IRGC corridor
→ 280 Indian seafarers in Gulf zone
→ Kharif fertiliser Gulf corridor
→ OMC crude import continuity
India hosts the Iranian FM while Trump meets Xi in Beijing.
Both tracks converge on Thursday. India is at the centre of both.

OMC HIKE: IMMINENT — THIS WEEK
Indian Oil + BPCL + HPCL: Rs 30,000 Cr/month losses.
Announcement expected Wednesday-Thursday before May 15.
Petrol near Rs 100/L in Delhi for first time ever.
Aramco CEO confirmed: even with deal, months before prices normalise.
The hike cannot wait for a deal that Aramco says won't fix prices anytime soon anyway.

VERDICT: Day 75 opens on the eve of the most consequential 48 hours of the 75-day war. Trump goes to Beijing with "piece of garbage" language and aides seriously considering combat resumption. Xi goes to Beijing knowing Iran's ambassador has been publicly telling him not to help Trump. Araghchi goes to Delhi to engage India while both summits happen simultaneously. And India's OMC is about to announce the biggest petrol price hike since the war began. Thursday and Friday will determine whether this war ends in weeks or extends into 2027 — which the Aramco CEO has now confirmed as the realistic alternative.
